intervals.label: proposal and design studies
intervals.note: Month from the 2026 project talk (2011.12); Physics World says it was first proposed in 2011 by Zhao Guangda. Design documents: Physics & Detector CDR (arXiv:2303.15790, 2023), accelerator CDR (arXiv:2509.11522, 2025). The accelerator CDR 'aims to secure support from the Chinese central government for its construction during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030)'; the June 2026 talk says the proposal was submitted in 2025 and defended for inclusion in that plan. No approval is reported in the sources fetched (as of 2026-10-26).

name: Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF)
notes: The Atlas marker is an area point in Hefei's Future Big Science City: the project talks name the city district as the site (about 1 km²) and show three candidate sites under geological exploration, so no tunnel site has been selected.
The accelerator CDR says construction would 'commence as planned in 2027 or 2028' if approved; that is a plan, recorded here as a note, not as an interval.
Budget figures in the project talks (about 4.5 to 4.98 billion CNY for construction, 364 to 400 million CNY for the key-technology R&D) are not recorded as specs.

circumference.note: Collider ring; the talks give 800 to 1000 m for earlier layouts.
circumference.quote: The STCF collider is a dual-ring machine with a circumference of about 860 m.

cms_energy.display: 7 GeV (upper end of the 2 to 7 GeV design range)
cms_energy.note: Upper end of the design range of 2 to 7 GeV.
cms_energy.quote: The main design goals of STCF are with a center-of-mass energy ranging from 2 to 7 GeV and a peak luminosity surpassing 5 × 10³⁴ cm⁻²s⁻¹ that is optimized at a center-of-mass energy of 4 GeV

peak_luminosity.display: above 5 × 10^34 cm^-2 s^-1 (design goal at 4 GeV)
peak_luminosity.note: A design goal ('surpassing'); the accelerator CDR's lattice studies also give about 1 × 10^35 cm^-2 s^-1 at a beam energy of 2 GeV.
peak_luminosity.quote: The main design goals of STCF are with a center-of-mass energy ranging from 2 to 7 GeV and a peak luminosity surpassing 5 × 10³⁴ cm⁻²s⁻¹ that is optimized at a center-of-mass energy of 4 GeV

summary.plain: A proposed electron-positron collider for the tau-charm energy region, 2 to 7 GeV, planned for Hefei, China, with about 50 times the luminosity of BEPCII. Its accelerator design report appeared in 2025; approval in China's 2026-2030 plan is pending and its site within Hefei is not yet chosen.
summary.technical: STCF: double-ring e⁺e⁻ collider with crab-waist collisions (ring about 860 m, linac injector with damping ring, top-up injection), √s = 2 to 7 GeV, design peak luminosity above 5×10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ at 4 GeV, optional polarised electron beam; Physics & Detector CDR 2023 (arXiv:2303.15790), accelerator CDR 2025 (arXiv:2509.11522); proposed 2011, key-technology R&D funded by Anhui, Hefei and USTC since 2023; seeking construction in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). Not approved in the sources fetched.
